meta.note: Article three-tile model. 01 OPENING = hook the reader (question hook or statement hook). 02 DEVELOPMENT = three moves drawn freely from four families: describe, compare, opinion, mini-story. 03 CLOSING = sign off with style (reflect, recommend or verdict). STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM REVIEWS: reviews assemble each line from slot fragments (background + hinge + aim, signpost + view + key + support). Articles do not decompose that way — an article has no rigid pattern, so the pools hold COMPLETE lines and the engine selects rather than assembles. There is no _join logic and no signpostJoin. Development is deliberately non-sequential: any three moves in any order is a valid article. Types are not subjects here; articles take any topic, so a single generic type is kept for envelope compatibility with the reviews reader.

Why do so many people attach such importance to … ?

There seems to be something irresistible about …
Few can resist the appeal of …
It's hard to deny that … plays a huge part in our lives.

describe: What makes it so special is …
compare: Apart from …, another thing that really stands out is …
opinion: One of the key things I love about … is …
For me personally, the best thing about … is …
As far as I'm concerned, … is of great importance.
ministory: I'll never forget the time when …
If I had to choose one example, it would be …

reflect: It's hard to imagine life without …
In short, there's something truly unforgettable about …
recommend: If you haven't tried / seen / experienced …, make sure you do — you won't regret it!
verdict: Whether you love it or not, there's no denying that … leaves a lasting impression.
